source_sections.title: The quay
source_sections.markdown:
At dusk Mara reached the quay with a letter she had promised not to read. The ferryman was called Leno. He looked once at the letter, and then at the river.

“There's still time to go back,” he said.

Mara put one foot into the boat. Behind her, a bell sounded from the town. A shuttered café across the street bore a peeling blue ship sticker: 🚢.

On the far bank, one window was already lit.

“There's still time to go back,” he said.

source_sections.title: The crossing
source_sections.markdown:
Leno steered into the mist. Mara asked whether the far bank had a name.

“Every place has a name,” he said. “Not every traveler needs to know it.”

The letter remained unopened in her pocket. The boat struck something in the dark and continued on.

When Mara looked back, the town had vanished.

sections.title: The quay
sections.markdown:
By the time Mara reached the quay, the light was fading. In her pocket was a letter she had promised not to open.

The ferryman, Leno, glanced at the letter and then at the river. “There's still time to go back,” he said.

Mara stepped into the boat. A bell rang behind her, somewhere in the town. Across the street, the shuttered café still had a blue ship sticker—🚢—peeling from its window.

On the opposite bank, a single window glowed in the dark.

sections.title: The crossing
sections.markdown:
Reno steered into the mist. Mara asked if the far bank had a name.

“Every place has a name,” he said. “Not every traveler needs to know it.”

She left the letter unopened in her pocket. Something knocked against the hull, then slipped away.

When she turned around, she could no longer see the town.
